assessment.summary: CD274 (PD-L1) is a highly validated immuno-oncology target with exceptional structural, chemical, and clinical evidence. Five approved antibody drugs exist, over 1,700 ChEMBL IC50 entries are recorded, and 80 PDB structures including sub-angstrom resolution co-crystal structures confirm a well-characterised binding interface. Druggability is high, though the dominant modality remains biologics; small-molecule inhibitors of the PD-1/PD-L1 interaction are an active but more challenging area.
evidence_gaps: Small-molecule druggability of the PD-1/PD-L1 protein-protein interface remains challenging; approved drugs are all monoclonal antibodies, and no small-molecule has yet reached approval
Median IC50 of ~210 nM in ChEMBL likely reflects a mix of antibody and small-molecule data; potency distribution for small molecules specifically is not disaggregated here
Resistance mechanisms (e.g., CD274 amplification, alternative checkpoint upregulation) are not fully characterised and may limit therapeutic durability
Tissue- and tumour-specific expression patterns and their impact on patient selection are still being refined
Combination therapy optimal partners and sequencing strategies remain an open clinical question
